Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our legal and security teams are asking for a concise excerpt we can attach to the SOW that explains exactly what Redwood stores by default:

- Are the raw user inputs/prompt fragments persisted anywhere by default (including streamed fragments)?
- Do you store intermediate KV cache snapshots or only final model outputs?
- If a customer requests deletion, what evidence and timeline do you provide?

If possible please provide a short paragraph we can include in the contract and an example row in a retention matrix (we'll want to store that as a Quick Reference). Can you also call out what is stored for troubleshooting vs what is stored for billing/metrics?

Asha — thanks for the clear asks. I pulled a short excerpt and a simple matrix that should be contract-ready (attached). Below is the concise language we recommend for the SOW plus a one-line example for your retention matrix.

SOW excerpt (suggested):
"By default Redwood retains request metadata and finalized model outputs for up to 45 days for operational troubleshooting and billing reconciliation. Raw user inputs (prompts) and streamed token fragments are treated as transient: streaming buffers and ephemeral prompt fragments are not persisted beyond the serving JVM/process unless explicitly flagged by the customer or captured via an enabled debug export. KV-cache snapshots used within an active session are in-memory artifacts; we do not persist KV-cache snapshots to durable storage by default. On approved erasure requests Redwood will remove persisted artifacts (finalized outputs and associated request metadata) and provide a deletion confirmation and log excerpt within 7 business days; billing records required for invoicing are retained per contract. Customers can opt into extended retention or residency controls in Dedicated/Private deployments."

Retention matrix example (single row):
- Item: Prompt fragments (streamed tokens) — Default retention: Ephemeral (not persisted) — Stored for: transient serving buffer only — Erasure: N/A (no durable copy)

I've attached the PDF excerpt and a one-page matrix (data-retention-matrix-northstar.xlsx). If Kim and Rishi want to tweak the legal wording I'll incorporate their changes.

Next steps: if you want hard evidence of deletion for audit, we can include an addendum that provides a time-stamped deletion log excerpt and the internal job run id that performed the purge. That is an optional add-on in our enterprise package.

— Soojin
Director, Security & Trust
Redwood Inference

Asha — quick answers from product/security:

1) Residency and centralized telemetry: by default, region-scoped hosted deployments keep customer request artifacts and finalized outputs in the region where the request is served. Platform health telemetry (aggregated metrics and anonymized error traces) may be forwarded to our central observability cluster for service health; those telemetry events do not contain prompt text or user inputs. For EU customers who require strict residency we recommend Redwood Private (VPC) or a Dedicated cluster with regional-only telemetry forwarding disabled.

2) Deletion confirmation: when we perform a customer-authorized purge we emit a signed deletion excerpt that includes: record id(s) removed, deletion job id, timestamp (RFC3339), artifact type (request metadata, finalized output), and region. Size is typically a few KB per purge job (depends on number of records). We do retain the signed deletion-excerpt entry in a secure audit ledger for 1 year to satisfy auditability and evidence-of-deletion needs; the ledger entry contains only metadata (no prompt text or output content). If Northstar requires proof-of-deletion without any ledger retention we can add a contractual clause to avoid ledger retention and provide a one-time signed deletion file instead.

I attached a slightly revised SOW paragraph that includes the residency and excerpt language (redwood-default-retention-excerpt-v1.2.pdf). If that looks good to you we can stitch into the SOW and have legal countersign.

Thanks — Kim
Sr. Product Security Manager
Redwood Inference
